subject: Measurement invariance longitudinal data -  number of items different at each time point

messages.author: 27c9b6fb55618875
messages.subject: Measurement invariance longitudinal data -  number of items different at each time point
parts:
Hi,

May I ask your help regarding measurement invariance of longitudinal data when the number of items varies across the time points?

I have data on bullying victimization at three time points using the same questionnaire. At the first two data points, 12 items are used and at the last data point only 6 items are used out of the 12 items used in previous waves. The response items are on a Likert scale from 0-2. I would like to check the measurement invariance across the 3 time points, but could not find any function for measurement invariance in which the number of items can be different at across the time points. Please could you guide me in the direction of a function/code for longitudinal invariance when the number of item at each time point is not identical? 

Thank you very much!

With kind regards,
Sinziana

messages.author: ad188126f9138663
messages.subject: Re: Measurement invariance longitudinal data - number of items different at each time point
parts:
Sinziana,
Your situation poses more of a psychometric problem than a syntax problem.  As I see it, you have two basic options in terms of the analysis.
(1) Conduct a 12-item analysis for the first two time points only, and a separate 6-item analysis for all three time points.
(2) Conduct a single analysis in which measurement invariance is imposed on 6 items across 3 time points and on 6 items across 2 time points.

The strength of the first analysis and weakness of the second analysis is that the 6 items that are not used in time 3 might change the interpretation of the latent variable, thus confounding the analysis a measurement invariance for the 6 items used in the third time point.  The first analysis avoids that.

The strength of the second analysis and weakness of the first analysis is that the construct measured by all 12 items is presumably what interests you and the second analysis focuses on that.  There is a degree of circularity involved in arguing that the items are invariant because of the parameters in the common factor model and the common factors are the same because of the invariant parameters.  However (drawing from an unpublished APA presentation) this is not necessarily a vicious circularity and conforms to the well accepted Hermeneutic Circle in which interpreters interpret parts of a text based on the whole and the whole based on the parts.

If it were me, I would probably run both analyses and compare the results as a form of sensitivity analysis.  There is nothing novel about the first set of analyses.  For the second, I would impose the 2-time constraints and the 3-time constraints in tandem as you work through the successive models.  Simply leave the missing 6 items out of the measurement model for the third time period.

Keith

Markus, K A. (2014).  Test Development and Validation Viewed as Mixed Methods Research.  A Critcal, Pluralist and Mixed-methods History of Measurement and Evaluaton in Psychology.  Symposium organized by Valerie Futch.  American Psychological Association.  August 2014, Washington D.C.

------------------------
Keith A. Markus
John Jay College of Criminal Justice, CUNY
http://jjcweb.jjay.cuny.edu/kmarkus

http://www.routledge.com/books/details/9781841692203/

messages.author: 27c9b6fb55618875
messages.subject: Re: Measurement invariance longitudinal data - number of items different at each time point
parts:
Hi Keith,

Thank you very much for your detailed answer! It was very useful as it made me think/analyse more seriously the items I am using and the purpose of the invariance analyses. 

I wanted to do the invariance analyses as a preliminary step, to make sure that I can use the measures at the three time points to derive developmental trajectories of bullying victimization using latent growth curve modeling. Looking more carefully at the questionnaire, I think the extra 6 items that are common only to wave 1 and 2, probably add important information to the construct of bullying victimization. However, I do not know how to test this. I suppose the easy way is to fit the LCGM with only the 6 items that are repeated over time. These 6 items have good measurement invariance over time. Ideally, I would like to make use of all the information available at T1 and T2, but not sure how to fit the LCGM to use all the information: 12 items at Time1, 12 items Time2 and 12 items Time3.

With many thanks and my best wishes,
Sinziana

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Measurement invariance longitudinal data - number of items different at each time point
parts: Ideally, I would like to make use of all the information available at T1 and T2, but not sure how to fit the LCGM to use all the information: 12 items at Time1, 12 items Time2 and 12 items Time3.

You can still include all 12 indicators at T1 and T2 (with invariance constraints) along with the 6 indicators at T3 (with invariance constraints).  There is nothing forcing you to have the same set of indicators at all occasions.  The latent scales can be linked with a few common indicators across occasions.

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Assistant Professor, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
http://www.uva.nl/profile/t.d.jorgensen
